extracted.subtask_description: A compilation of Associated Press dispatches from late December 1945 covering international and domestic postwar developments (military movements, United Nations delegation/site selection, labor disputes, repatriation and related policy actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: UNO site distance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision specified that the site must not be nearer than 5 miles or farther than 80 A from New York or be within ile radius of Bos (committee eliminated Springfield, Mass., and Cape Cod under that decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion was applied by the interim committee when winnowing possible permanent United Nations sites; Hyde Park and Boston remained after application of this distance/radius rule. (Original text is garbled on exact '80 A' and 'ile radius' wording.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission for Tokyo electro-technical laboratory with research restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Allied headquarters granted the Japanese government permission to operate an electro-technical laboratory in Tokyo, but with strict provisions against research in certain fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The item lists prohibited research areas in the security-sensitive fields, including 'television, radio and radar countermeasures', 'pulse modulated multi-channel communications systems', 'proximity devices', 'voice secrecy systems (speech scramblers)', and 'electronic code and cipher systems.' The permission is conditional and explicitly restricts those research areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness-production requests must be made through counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: The American reply to Tojo assured that 'full consideration will be given to requests for production of witnesses on behalf of General ... when such request is made through his counsel.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for witnesses to testify on behalf of the accused will be considered only if submitted via the accused's legal counsel—i.e., a procedural requirement governing production of witnesses in connection with war-crimes proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement of State Department booklet release upon protest
rubrics_metrics.description: Following a protest by Reuter, the State Department postponed publication of the booklet on the suggested postwar international information program and promised to release simultaneously any statement submitted by Reuter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a party lodges a formal protest alleging factual errors or libel, the department delayed release (from Dec. 29 to Jan. 5) to allow the protested party to prepare and submit a response for simultaneous publication; the department read the protest letter and its own statement at a news conference and declined further amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family-permit proportionality policy for service members overseas
rubrics_metrics.description: When/if family reunification in China is authorized, 'permits will be given wives of enlisted men in exact proportion to those given officers' wives.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy governing issuance of permits for wives and families to join service members overseas will mirror the proportion already provided to officers' wives, reflecting a proportional allocation rule tied to rank-based precedents and considerations such as housing, heat, schools and logistical constraints.
